debrief.whyItWorks: With limited clock, taking space while the defence is unsettled is the most reliable way to plant in time. Here, 3 players faced 2 with about 35 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It spends the team's options at once, leaving little for the post-plant.
debrief.assumption: The defenders cannot rotate enough players to the site before the plant.
debrief.breaksWhen: The defence stacks the chosen site and has its own utility ready for the execute.

evidenceReview.explanation: The team had no utility left. The utility left sets how much of the plan can be forced rather than hoped for.
The round clock stood near 35 seconds. The round clock bounds how long any plan can take.
It was 3 players against 2. The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan.
The last-seen position of one defender in CT Spawn was about 6 seconds old. A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age.
The last-seen position of one defender in CT Spawn was about 13 seconds old. A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age.

debrief.followupReview: No decisive new information arrived, so the answers are scored close together; the best-supported answer was: Stick to the line you chose.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to send a single lurker behind the defence, playing a player down for a thinner site defence.

counterfactual.changedFact: The defenders are known to be stacked on the site you would hit.
counterfactual.effect: The execute meets a full defence, and taking information or faking becomes stronger.
